summary: Closed the run's one dangling registration — @lease_transfer_bypass, the question I filed last turn — with a source-based interpretation rather than leaving it unanswered or filing an experiment that no remaining turn could interpret. The mechanism is settled by reading: the lease is written as force := bytes.Equal(m.GetContext(), []byte(campaignTransfer)), and a higher-term MsgVote or MsgPreVote is discarded only when force is false and inLease holds, so a request carrying that marker is answered — the receiver adopts the higher term, becomes a follower with r.lead = None, and then applies canVote and isUpToDate. The marker has exactly one producer in the snapshot: campaign() sets it only when t == campaignTransfer, the campaign entered from stepFollower's MsgTimeoutNow case via r.hup(campaignTransfer), which increments the term and sends MsgVote at the new term. Two consequences matter for how the lease should be read: the bypass is narrow by construction, since a node campaigning on its own — including a stale one — never carries the marker, which is why the lease withheld the vote in every receipt of the main account; and the trust it rests on is a statement about the sender, because the receiver keeps no record of a pending transfer and the context field is neither authenticated nor compared with local state. That second point decides the judgment, and it is the same shape as the term-less network message already refuted: a sender claiming an internal precondition it does not hold sits outside the crash-fault model, and the snapshot states no duty to verify a claimed transfer. I recorded it as explained with the defect claim refuted, cited the new behaviour entry as a knowledge use with the specific assertion it supports, and left the registered discriminator intact so a future run can measure it in one probe. Before closing I re-verified the whole record: every receipt cited by any interpretation or knowledge entry exists, every cited index falls inside its receipt's event count, and every cited source is a captured material — problems: none, across fifteen distinct receipts, thirteen questions, twenty-three knowledge entries and zero gaps. Update validates with execution_requested=false, and nothing is left uncited.
